title: fix(app-shell): a field-backed action param reaches its record picker, and an unreadable one is refused
body:
Fixes #10129

Clause-②: no — `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over this branch's 16 paths answers `NOT GOVERNED — none matched`. The diff is `packages/app-shell`, `packages/core`, `packages/i18n` and one changeset; it touches no `AGENTS.md`, no `CLAUDE.md`, nothing under `.claude/**`, `skills/**` or `docs/adr/**`.

## Step 1 first: which side dropped the binding

The card refused to name a side and asked for one to be established. **Outcome: the binding reaches the client, and the renderer path ignores it.** The fix is here, in this repo.

The decision site is `paramToField()` in `packages/app-shell/src/utils/paramToField.ts` — the `paramDegradesWithoutTarget(param)` branch that rewrites `type` to `'text'`. But that is not where this defect lives, and finding that out is most of the work: for the reported param that branch **never fires**.

One step earlier, `resolveActionParam()` in `packages/app-shell/src/utils/resolveActionParams.ts` resolves a field-backed param against the `objects` list its **caller** hands it:

```ts
const owner = ctx.objects.find((o) => o?.name === ownerName);
const field: RuntimeField | undefined = owner?.fields?.[param.field];
if (!field) { /* … type: param.type ?? 'text' … */ }
```

A field-backed param (`{ field: 'contract_type' }`) declares no inline `type`, so when the owner object is absent from that list the param becomes a `text` param — before any picker logic runs. Measured on this tree, both before and after the change:

| resolver input | resolved `type` | `referenceTo` | `paramDegradesWithoutTarget` | widget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{ field }`, owner object present | `lookup` | `clm_contract_type` | false | `lookup` |
| `{ field }`, owner object **absent** | `text` | undefined | **false** | `text` |
| `{ name, type: 'lookup', reference }` inline | `lookup` | `clm_contract_type` | false | `lookup` |

Row 2 is the card, in every detail. `paramDegradesWithoutTarget` answering **false** is the load-bearing half: by the time anything downstream looks, the param *is* a `text` param, and text params do not degrade. So no "no reference target" warning fired, the "paste a record id" placeholder and help text (#3405) did not apply, and the user got an unannotated empty box — no dropdown, no typeahead, and **no request for the referenced object on the wire, because no picker was ever built**. That silence is why this survived a version.

### Which callers cannot hold the right list

- `packages/app-shell/src/console/ConsoleShell.tsx` — `GlobalActionRuntimeProvider` calls `useConsoleActionRuntime({ dataSource })` with **no** `objects` and **no** `objectName`. Its own docblock says why it exists: every `action:button` *outside* ObjectView / RecordDetailView / PageView / DeclaredActionsBar binds to it, and it was added so a `type: 'flow'` action there stops failing with "Flow handler not registered". The card's action is a flow trigger (`POST /api/v1/automation/contract_intake/trigger`).
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/DeclaredActionsBar.tsx` — `objects: objectDef ? [objectDef] : []`. One object, so any `objectOverride` param misses; and when the bar is driven by its `actions` prop, `useMetadataItem('object', undefined)` leaves `objectDef` undefined and the list is empty.
- `ObjectView` and `RecordDetailView` pass the full list and were never affected.

### What the server serves, versus what the record form gets

Read in `/home/user/objectstack` (read-only; nothing was committed, pushed or opened there):

- `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` — `ActionParamSchema` is `strictObject`, and its own docblock names the two declaration modes: field-backed `{ field }`, and inline, where "a `lookup` / `master_detail` param declared this way MUST name its target object via `reference`". So for a **field-backed** param the server serves no object binding *on the param at all*, and is not supposed to: the binding lives on the object's field def, and the client already holds it.
- `packages/spec/src/ui/action-params.zod.ts` — "Field-backed params are resolved to their effective value-shape inputs by the CALLER (the runtime, which holds the object metadata registry)". The client side of that same contract is `resolveActionParams`, and its registry is `useMetadata().objects`.
- `packages/spec/src/conversions/registry.ts`, `field-reference-to-alias` — the serve path canonicalises a stored `reference_to` to `reference` so objectui may delete its fallback arms. That interlock is intact here: `normalizeSchemaReferenceKeys` still stamps both spellings at ingestion in `MetadataProvider`, and a control leg confirms a def carrying only `reference_to` resolves its target once it has been through that door.

⇒ the object binding is on the client, in the same store the record form reads. The action-param seam simply never asked the store for it. ⛔ Nothing in the server's contract had to change, and nothing upstream is filed.

## The lit control

`legD` in the new pin file drives two paths in one run, against the same field def:

- **record form** — the object's `contract_type` def handed to the shared field widget the form renders. Clicking the trigger queries `clm_contract_type` and offers its records. This is the card's "it works there in this same build", measured here rather than quoted.
- **action param, through the console runtime** — `useConsoleActionRuntime({ dataSource })`, `ConsoleShell`'s supply verbatim, under a metadata store that has the object. Same outcome now: a picker, a query naming `clm_contract_type`, and options offered.

With the supply half reverted, the second leg alone goes red and the record-form control stays green — which is the difference the card asked to be located.

## The change

1. **`useConsoleActionRuntime`** resolves field-backed params against the caller's objects unioned with the metadata store's, **caller first** (`withKnownObjects`, exported beside the resolver with its own docblock). A draft or preview overlay the caller carries still wins on any name it defines. The handler awaits `ensureType('object')` first — it is already promise-returning by contract — so "this field does not exist" is an answer and not a cold-boot race, which is what makes the refusal below sound.
2. **`resolveActionParam`** stamps `unresolvedField` (the `OBJECT.FIELD` pair, as a string) when it cannot read a field-backed param, and says so in dev. The last-resort `text` shape stays — a partially cached console must not crash — but it no longer travels anonymously.
3. **`ActionParamDialog`** refuses such a param: an alert naming the pair in place of the control, a `console.error` per dialog opening **in every build**, and a disabled Confirm so the action cannot be launched with a value the dialog had no contract to collect. The refusal is deliberately not gated on `required` — a param that cannot be read is a broken declaration either way, and a silent optional one is the same invisible failure a submit later.

`actionDialog.unresolvedParam` is added to all ten locale bundles. The `OBJECT.FIELD` locator renders as its own node rather than an interpolation, so an identifier is never re-ordered by a translation.

## Evidence

Pins: `packages/app-shell/src/views/ActionParamDialog.fieldBackedPickerReach-10129.test.tsx` — 13 passing, four legs, every leg with a control beside it.

Reverse verification. Each leg mutated one file on disk, proved the mutation by blob hash (and for the surgical one, by an occurrence count that had to move `1 -> 0`), ran the pins, then restored with `git checkout HEAD -- path` and proved the restore by an empty `git diff HEAD` — never by an exit code. A `trap … EXIT INT TERM` carried the restore. Run from the committed fix, so the red and green numbers are about committed bytes.

| ablation | result |
|---|---|
| revert `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` to the branch base | **1 failed**, 12 passed — only "the picker renders and QUERIES the referenced object, from the supply ConsoleShell really uses" |
| revert `ActionParamDialog.tsx` to the branch base | **2 failed**, 11 passed — both refusal legs, `Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="param-unresolved-contract_type"]` |
| delete only the `unresolvedField` emit from the resolver | **4 failed**, 9 passed — `expected undefined to be 'clm_contract.contract_type'`, plus both refusal legs |
| restored | 13 passed, `git diff HEAD` empty |

Local checks, all run from the repository root after the merge of `origin/main` at `6cae9a0b3`, against `6d4f4da96`:

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/ packages/core/src/actions/ packages/i18n/` — `Test Files 837 passed (837)`, `Tests 8925 passed | 1 skipped (8926)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core --filter @object-ui/app-shell --filter @object-ui/i18n type-check` — exit 0, after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`.
- `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` — all exit 0.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` and `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — exit 0.
- `check:eager-locale-catalogues` and `check:eager-closure` — exit 0 after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/console...' build`. The tenth locale key adds nothing eager: the nine non-`en` catalogues stay on demand and `en` stays the only resident one. ⛔ No ceiling in `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` was touched.

Lint, as a declared narrowing rather than a repo-wide run. `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the five changed `.ts`/`.tsx` sources: exit 0, `0 errors`, 76 warnings, **0 of them new** — the two `react-hooks/refs` warnings in the report are the pre-existing `serverActionEnvRef` pair, not this diff's. The population is what `eslint.config.js` itself configures, the file count is read off `--format json` (5), and the narrowing is sound because this repo does not enable type-aware linting: no `parserOptions.project` and no `projectService` appear in `eslint.config.js`, so nothing in this diff can move a verdict on a file it did not touch. The full repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config` is CI's run, not this branch's.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, observed, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not changed here:

- `RecordDetailView` builds a **second**, near-identical `paramCollectionHandler` that does not go through the store union. It is not a defect today — that view receives the full `objects` list as a prop, which is why it was never in the reported path — but the two handlers are documented as a pair that must not drift (`RecordDetailView.paramRuntimeParity-6431.test.tsx`), and they now differ by this union. Successor: whoever next edits either handler; the pin file names both.
- `RuntimeField` in `resolveActionParams.ts` still declares `reference_to`, which no read in that file consumes any more (objectui#6837 narrowed the read to `reference`). Dead declaration, no behavioural effect — ingestion canonicalises both spellings.

⛔ The card's two further dialog defects — no max-height / internal scroll, and the file widget posting a browser blob — are each their own card and neither is touched here.
